ranking_rule: Pairwise/score-based scientific priority using theory coherence, falsifiability, empirical testability, data feasibility, identification feasibility, information gain, economic importance, and replication feasibility; never p-value optimization.

candidates.claim: Official archive vintages around the FIZ-to-CIZ transition exhibit economically non-trivial measurement sensitivity in factor and/or portfolio return series.
candidates.counterclaim: Vintage differences are economically negligible relative to ordinary monthly variation.

candidates.claim: Holding the historical calendar and model specification fixed, some CAPM/FF3/FF5 empirical conclusions are sensitive to archive vintage.
candidates.counterclaim: Model signs, significance classifications, and alpha magnitudes are stable across vintages.

candidates.claim: The inferred effective factor dimension can differ across vintages under a reduced-rank framework.
candidates.counterclaim: The inferred factor dimension is stable across vintages.

candidates.claim: Revision sensitivity is heterogeneous across factors, portfolios, and historical subperiods rather than uniform.
candidates.counterclaim: Revision sensitivity is approximately homogeneous across series and subperiods.

candidates.claim: Apparent mean-revision evidence weakens materially after multiplicity control for families of tests.
candidates.counterclaim: Key revision signals remain statistically reliable after FDR control.

candidates.claim: The two-vintage difference cannot by itself identify the pure causal effect of FIZ-to-CIZ because ordinary archive revisions are a competing channel.
candidates.counterclaim: All observed archive differences can be attributed to FIZ-to-CIZ alone.

meta_review.reason: The primary package can measure sensitivity and conclusion stability immediately. Pure causal attribution requires an additional decomposition design.
